text:
sylvia: Noticing a spike in onboarding issues: sample quickstart users hitting high latency + soft-429s when they start multiple paginated workers. Looks like client-side token bucket logic in the JS SDK is too permissive with burst windows.
ben: We're seeing this in logs: many clients acquire cursors and immediately spawn N workers. Token bucket refills allow short bursts that oversubscribe dedicated pools.
omar: Is this different from the semaphore/leasing problem? Feels related but distinct: this is about smoothing bursts, not leaking.
sylvia: Right. Two separate but compounding problems: (A) leaking leases in a few older samples, and (B) bursty acquisitions without backpressure. The result is a queue that fills and then we return soft 429s which trigger aggressive client retries -> thundering herd.
ben: Quick repro script I used (JS):
```js
// naive parallel paginator
for await (const page of paginator) {
  // spawn processing concurrently
  workerPool.spawn(() => doWork(page));
}
```
This paired with tokenBucket allowing bursts of 50 -> 200 inflight briefly.
omar: Proposed mitigations: 1) sample quickstart change to show a "bounded" concurrency pattern with a small helper (maxConcurrent + backoff), 2) SDK enhancement: expose a configurable smoothing window + leaky-bucket mode, 3) docs: clear guidance for production pagination patterns.
sylvia: I like adding a small helper to the SDKs (TS/Go/Py) — opt-in, simple API: client.withBackpressure({maxConcurrent, warmupMs}) that returns acquire/release. Should be easy to wire in quickstart.
docs-bot: Note: Python SDK already exports AsyncLimiter (context mgr). JS has a community snippet but no official helper.
ben: Parity is important here. Let's ensure Go/TS offer same semantics and similar defaults. Defaults: maxConcurrent = 8, warmupMs = 5000? Open to bikeshedding.
omar: Also need to fix retry behavior: when we get a 429 the SDK retries but does not adjust the token bucket or decrement counters for the failed attempt before the retry, so effective concurrency spikes. Fix: on all retry/backoff paths, call release() or decrement in-flight counters before scheduling retry.
sylvia: Agreed. Tests: add a unit test that simulates 100 rapid acquire attempts with server returning intermittent 429s and assert that in-flight never exceeds configured max by more than 1.
ben: For the quickstart, I'll drop in a minimal backpressure helper example:
```js
const limiter = client.backpressure({maxConcurrent: 16});
for await (const page of paginator) {
  await limiter.acquire();
  process(page).finally(() => limiter.release());
}
```
omar: Telemetry: surface a metric `client.inflight` emitted every 10s and a histogram of burst durations. Console should show warning if inflight > maxConcurrent for >15s. That will let us catch leaks vs bursts.
sylvia: UX note: onboarding emails and quickstart should call out the helper prominently. Many users copy/paste quickstarts and assume it's production-ready.
docs-bot: Filed DOCREQ-884: add backpressure guide and quickstart snippet.
ben: Implementation plan: 1) patch quickstart in sample-app repo with helper and finally example (hotfix), 2) change JS SDK to export `backpressure` helper + adjust retry paths to decrement, 3) mirror change in Go + Py SDKs for parity, 4) add telemetry and console warning (follow-on).
omar: I'll own the JS SDK PR. Ben can do Go. Sylvia will coordinate docs.
ci-bot: CI: branch `feat/backpressure-helper` created, tests queued.
sylvia: We should also add a short note about auth retries: some customers use short-lived tokens and refresh flows; when token refresh fails during retry we should not hold slots indefinitely. Ensure acquire/release interacts with auth refresh paths.
ben: Good call. Add a test that simulates token refresh failure mid-retry and assert release happens.
omar: Also, add a small e2e with Dedicated: spin up small dedicated pool and run quickstart to validate SLOs under burst. This will catch config regressions.
ci-bot: CI: `feat/backpressure-helper` tests failed (integration: 3/12 flaky). Reporting to PR.
sylvia: Let's triage failures tomorrow. For now, update the docs to warn about copying naive concurrency patterns. Thanks all, this should reduce onboarding friction significantly.
ben: PR numbers: sampleapp PR#710, js-sdk PR#711, go-sdk PR#712, docs PR#2212. I'll tag them in the channel when opened. :white_check_mark:
